pharm: Chemotherapy rescue / antidote / folate replacement; 5-FU modulator
quick: Methotrexate rescue ~15 mg (10 mg/m2) q6h x10 doses; high-dose per MTX level
Oral may be taken with or without food; high doses given IV
Used when benefit justifies risk (e.g. with methotrexate toxicity/antidotes)
Delayed methotrexate clearance needs higher/longer leucovorin; adjust to MTX level
Methotrexate level, creatinine, CBC, mucositis; CMV/response in colorectal regimens
summary: Leucovorin calcium (folinic acid) is a reduced folate that does not require dihydrofolate reductase for activation, so it bypasses the block produced by folate-antagonist drugs. It is used to 'rescue' normal cells after high-dose methotrexate, as an antidote to methotrexate/other folate-antagonist overdose, to treat folate-deficiency megaloblastic anaemia when oral folate cannot be used, and to potentiate fluorouracil in colorectal cancer. Do NOT use it alone to treat pernicious anaemia (it can produce a haematologic response while neurologic damage progresses).
indications: Rescue therapy after high-dose methotrexate in osteosarcoma
To diminish toxicity and counteract effects of inadvertent overdosage of folic acid antagonists (e.g. methotrexate)
Treatment of megaloblastic anaemia due to folate deficiency when oral therapy is not feasible
In combination with fluorouracil to prolong survival in palliative metastatic colorectal cancer

dosage.d: 15 mg (about 10 mg/m2) orally/IM/IV every 6 hours for 10 doses, starting 24 h after methotrexate
dosage.n: Adjust dose/duration to serum methotrexate level and creatinine

dosage.d: Increase leucovorin (e.g. up to 100 mg/m2 IV q3-6h) until MTX <0.05 micromolar
dosage.n: Continue with hydration and urinary alkalinisation; do not give it intrathecally

dosage.d: Give as soon as possible; up to ~75 mg IV then 12 mg IM q6h x4 (or per MTX-overdose protocol)
dosage.n: Efficacy falls sharply if delayed beyond ~1 hour
No benefit beyond 1 mg/day; use when oral folic acid not feasible

dosage.d: 20 mg/m2 IV (or 200 mg/m2) before 5-FU, per regimen (e.g. daily x5, repeated)
dosage.n: Leucovorin potentiates 5-FU toxicity as well as efficacy - monitor

admin: May be given orally, IM or IV; for doses above 25 mg use the parenteral route (oral absorption is saturable)
When used as methotrexate rescue, start at the scheduled time (usually 24 h after MTX) - do not delay, and continue per methotrexate levels with hydration and urinary alkalinisation
Reconstitute parenteral product per instructions; for neonates avoid diluents containing benzyl alcohol
moa: Leucovorin is a reduced, already-active form of folate (5-formyltetrahydrofolate) that is readily converted to other tetrahydrofolate cofactors. Because it does not need reduction by dihydrofolate reductase, it bypasses the enzyme blockade caused by folate-antagonist drugs (methotrexate, trimethoprim, pyrimethamine), restoring folate-dependent one-carbon metabolism in normal cells. With fluorouracil, it stabilises the FdUMP-thymidylate synthase complex, enhancing 5-FU cytotoxicity.

absolute: Pernicious anaemia and other megaloblastic anaemias secondary to vitamin B12 deficiency (improper therapy)
Known hypersensitivity to leucovorin or folinic acid products
relative: Concurrent fluorouracil in debilitated patients (enhanced 5-FU toxicity, including fatal GI toxicity)
Effusions/third-space fluid that delay methotrexate clearance

preg: There are no adequate controlled studies; leucovorin is generally used when clearly needed, particularly to manage methotrexate toxicity. With 5-FU regimens, the cytotoxic partner governs pregnancy risk. Use when the benefit justifies the risk.
lact: It is not known whether leucovorin is excreted in human milk; use with caution. With antineoplastic regimens, breastfeeding is generally not recommended.
renal: Renal impairment or any cause of delayed methotrexate excretion increases methotrexate exposure and requires higher and/or more prolonged leucovorin dosing, guided by the serum methotrexate level, together with hydration and urinary alkalinisation.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is established for leucovorin itself.

major: Methotrexate - leucovorin rescues normal cells; inadequate or delayed dosing risks fatal methotrexate toxicity (and excessive dosing can blunt antitumour effect of high-dose MTX)
Fluorouracil - leucovorin potentiates both efficacy and toxicity (severe diarrhoea, mucositis, myelosuppression) - 5-FU dose may need reduction
moderate: Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole / pyrimethamine - leucovorin may reduce antimicrobial/antiparasitic efficacy (e.g. in PCP or Pneumocystis treatment) - use with caution
Phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone - leucovorin/folates may lower antiepileptic levels and increase seizure frequency
interactions.food: Oral leucovorin may be taken with or without food; high doses require parenteral administration.
interactions.diagnostics: Used with serum methotrexate monitoring to guide rescue; corrects megaloblastic indices.

serious: Severe (potentially fatal) GI toxicity with fluorouracil (especially elderly/debilitated)
rare: Increased seizure frequency in susceptible children
emergency: Life-threatening GI toxicity or myelosuppression with 5-FU

monitoring: Serum methotrexate level to guide rescue dose and duration
Serum creatinine, urine output and urine pH during high-dose MTX
CBC and mucositis/diarrhoea, especially with fluorouracil regimens
Electrolytes and hydration with 5-FU combination therapy
counsel: This 'folinic acid' protects your normal cells from methotrexate - take or receive every dose exactly on time
Drink plenty of fluids during high-dose methotrexate treatment as advised
With 5-fluorouracil, report diarrhoea, mouth sores or signs of infection promptly - these can become serious
Do not stop or delay rescue doses without contacting your cancer team
Tell your doctor about epilepsy medicines or antibiotics like co-trimoxazole
pk: Rescue effect begins promptly after administration
Active 5-methyltetrahydrofolate peaks within ~1-2 h (oral) / sooner IV
Dosed every 3-6 hours during rescue/antidote protocols
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from light; reconstituted solution per stability limits
pearls: Folinic acid (leucovorin), NOT folic acid, is the agent used for methotrexate rescue and folate-antagonist overdose - it bypasses dihydrofolate reductase
Start rescue on time and titrate to the serum methotrexate level; delayed/inadequate rescue can be fatal
Potentiates fluorouracil efficacy AND toxicity - watch for severe diarrhoea/mucositis, reduce 5-FU if needed
Improper for B12-deficiency anaemia - corrects blood counts while neurologic damage progresses
Levoleucovorin (the L-isomer) is dosed at half the leucovorin (racemic) dose - do not confuse the two
missed: Rescue and antidote doses are time-critical - never skip or delay a methotrexate-rescue dose. If a dose is missed, contact the treating team immediately, as additional doses or methotrexate-level checks may be required.
overdose: Excessive leucovorin is generally well tolerated but can negate the antineoplastic effect of co-administered folate antagonists (e.g. high-dose methotrexate) and may worsen fluorouracil toxicity. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care and reassess the chemotherapy regimen.
